root_cause.text: nouveau’s DP AUX transfer path in `nouveau_connector_aux_xfer()` did not check whether the GPU was runtime-suspended, so userspace `/dev/drm_dp_*` accesses could issue AUX RPCs to the GSP while the device was asleep, leading to the crash in `r535_gsp_msgq_wait()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (pm_runtime_suspended(nv_connector->base.dev->dev)) return -EBUSY;` at the start of `nouveau_connector_aux_xfer()`, and the CVE says the bug happens “If we have runtime suspended, and userspace wants to use /dev/drm_dp_* then just tell it the device is busy instead of crashing in the GSP code,” with the observed warning in `r535_gsp_msgq_wait+0x9a/0xb0`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (pm_runtime_suspended(nv_connector->base.dev->dev)) return -EBUSY;` at the start of `nouveau_connector_aux_xfer()`, and the CVE says the bug happens “If we have runtime suspended, and userspace wants to use /dev/drm_dp_* then just tell it the device is busy instead of crashing in the GSP code,” with the observed warning in `r535_gsp_msgq_wait+0x9a/0xb0`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a runtime-suspend check to block DP AUX transfers when the device is not active.
intent_record.what: In nouveau_connector_aux_xfer(), a new early return was added before encoder lookup: if pm_runtime_suspended(nv_connector->base.dev->dev) is true, the function now returns -EBUSY.
intent_record.how: This prevents DP AUX transfers from proceeding while the device is runtime-suspended, avoiding access to hardware that is not currently powered or available and causing callers to retry or defer the operation.

grouping_result.intent: Add a runtime-suspend check to block DP AUX transfers when the device is not active.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it adds a runtime-suspend/active-state check to prevent DP AUX transfers when the GPU is asleep, which addresses the missing guard that allowed AUX RPCs to reach the GSP and crash.

candidates.rationale: This is the start of the DP AUX transfer path in nouveau_connector_aux_xfer(); before the fix, execution continued from here without any runtime-suspend check, allowing AUX requests to reach the GSP even when the GPU was asleep.
This pre-fix conditional shows the only immediate gating was whether a DP encoder existed, not whether the device was runtime-active, which is the missing validation behind the crash.
This return only handles absence of a DP encoder; it does not protect against runtime-suspended hardware, so the vulnerable path remained reachable when the GPU was asleep.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the start of the AUX transfer path in nouveau_connector_aux_xfer(); pre-fix, it proceeded from this point without any runtime-suspend check, allowing userspace AUX requests to reach the GSP while the GPU was asleep.
This conditional only checks whether a DP encoder exists. It does not verify that the device is runtime-active, so it failed to block AUX RPCs on a suspended GPU.
This return only handles the missing-encoder case and leaves the runtime-suspended case unguarded, which is the root cause of the crash path.
